web_evidence.title: Fall of Giants — official extract
web_evidence.note: The sustained 21-page extract hosted on Ken Follett's official site narrates Billy externally as he/him while entering his private fears and perceptions, establishing third-person limited narration in the opening.

web_evidence.title: Baccalauréat Général, Anglais LV1 2016 — Fall of Giants extract
web_evidence.note: The examination reproduces a sustained 1917 interior passage around Ethel in third person, confirming that q01638 belongs to base narration rather than an embedded voice.

web_evidence.title: Ken Follett Writing Styles in Fall of Giants
web_evidence.note: The point-of-view section explicitly describes the whole novel as using one third-person narrator across eight focal characters, predominantly in third-person limited mode.

web_evidence.title: Excerpt from Fall of Giants by Ken Follett
web_evidence.note: This sustained excerpt, published by permission of Penguin Books, independently presents Billy and his family through external third-person narration and Billy's internal perspective.

person_note: The controlling narrator is nonparticipating and uses third person while shifting focalization among characters. Several supplied interior passages unmistakably present Walter, Gus, and Ethel externally while conveying their private thoughts or intentions; the official opening extract shows the same construction, and the whole-book POV source explicitly says the narrator remains third person across eight focal characters. The isolated I-lines in q01628 and q01629 are clipped character utterances and probable upstream event-bucket errors, while q01645 is embedded Shakespearean language; none establishes a first-person section. The main limitation is that the authorized extracts do not cover the entire novel, but the independent interior evidence and explicit whole-book description resolve that coverage gap without credible contrary evidence.
